Halcyon.title: Halcyon
Halcyon.extract:
Halcyon is a level 118 Mythic Wand. It can be found in Loot Chests and dropped by mobs of level 114 to 122.
Halcyon requires  Dexterity,  Intelligence, and  Agility, and is designed for the Light Bender Mage archetype. It is generally incompatible with  Strength, but provides damage in all five Elements. Its unique Major ID, Blinding Lights, drastically buffs the user's Ophanim orbs but causes them to orbit the user like Lightweaver orbs, constantly inflicting damage and Crystallize stacks to nearby enemies rather than functioning at long range.

Architect requires  Strength,  Intelligence, and  Defense, and is designed for the Trickster Assassin archetype. Architect has a world interaction with a particular shrine in the Industrial District.

Canary.title: Canary
Canary.extract: The Canary is the tritagonist of the level 85 Quest The Canary Calls, while its hallucination is the main antagonist of the quest. In the quest, Chief Clight learns of a gas leak in the Thesead Coal Mines, which will impact the coal mining industry harshly in the aforementioned town. He requests the player to investigate the leak with the Canary, who as Clight describes it, the mascot of the mining crew. After the player frees the Canary from the cage, the duo goes down into the mines to investigate the leak. However, after reaching an abandoned part of the mine, the Canary dies from the gas, while the player starts seeing a more eldritch form of it when looking for a way out. After the player progresses further into the mines, they wander aimlessly as their mind starts to deteriorate, before they are jumpscared by the Canary. It talks to them in a sadistic way, asking them to join them in death. After they refuse, it then brings the player to an arena where they do battle each other. After the Canary is defeated, it asks the player to end its existence, and will either die or remain in the player's mind forever. After the hallucination's fate had been decided, they wake up after the Thesead Coal Miners perform CPR on the player.

Albatross.title: Albatross
Albatross.extract:
Albatross is a level 104 Legendary Necklace. It can be found in Tier 3 [✫✫✫✫] and Tier 4 [✫✫✫✫] Loot Chests from levels 100 to 108.
Albatross is a Heavy Melee item that requires moderate investment in the Dexterity and Defense skills, fitting well in  ETF or  TFA builds. It provides Attack Speed reduction and a very large bonus to Main Attack Damage in all five elements (though reduced  Water damage overall), in exchange for an increase in movement spell cost.

Pandemonium can only be worn after completing the  ??? Quest. It is the only item in the game with the Major ID of Madness, which forces its wearer to cast a random ability every 3 seconds from any powder special and any class' main attack or spells at no mana cost. You can still use attacks and cast spells as usual in between these random castings.

Fatal.title: Fatal
Fatal.extract:
Fatal is a level 99 Mythic Wand. It can be found in Loot Chests and dropped by mobs of level 95 to 103.
Fatal's  Thunder damage is highly variable, and the lack of Neutral damage may be problematic against mobs who heavily resist or are immune to  Thunder; however, it gives powerful damage bonuses to spells, as well as a large buff to Dexterity, further increasing damage dealt. The wand also increases the player's Heal spell cost, but decreases the player's Teleport spell cost.
Fatal can be Ascended at an Item Upgrader in exchange for various Wards, boosting its combat level to 111 and increasing its base damage and Identifications.

Warp.title: Warp
Warp.extract:
Warp is a level 99 Mythic Wand. It can be found in Loot Chests and dropped by mobs of level 95-103.
Warp is the highest base damage wand in the game, but it is not recommended to use in combat, as with its massive downsides, including its 125 Agility requirement, which can be sometimes very restrictive to Warp builds, as there can not be enough Skill Points to use certain items. Instead, the weapon is mostly used in mobility and lootrun builds due to its massive Walk Speed and -2nd Spell Cost buffs.

The Parasite.title: The Parasite
The Parasite.extract:
The Parasite is a dark creature originating from the Realm of Dern. It was sent to Gavel Province from Dern in order to leech the Province's light, and is the progenitor of the parasitic Hatchlings, which are responsible for draining the light and spreading the Decay throughout the northwestern regions of the Province. After establishing a foothold of Decay in Gavel, it departed and infected Orphion himself, the embodiment of the Realm of Light.
The Parasite and its Hatchlings are directly or indirectly involved in numerous Quests in Gavel, as well as the Secret Discoveries added throughout the Province in the 1.20 Gavel Reborn Update. It ultimately appears as the final boss of Orphion's Nexus of Light, a Raid in the Realm of Light unlocked after completing the fifth and final part of the Realm of Light questline.

Slayer.title: Slayer
Slayer.extract:
Slayer is a pair of level 94 Mythic Boots. It can be found in Loot Chests and dropped by mobs of level 90-98.
It gives many good buffs all around, most notably the -3rd Spell Cost, +1 Tier Attack Speed and +Main Attack Damage Raw. Due to these buffs, the boots are most commonly used on Fast Hybrid builds, where it is a very useful item. Just because of the -3rd spell cost alone, the item is also utilized in spell builds, mainly zero-Intelligence spell.
The main debuff the boots give is a moderate amount of negative Health Regen. On the contrary, the boots have a bit of Stealing, which can be used with items such as Old Keeper's Ring or The Jingling Jester to activate the Greed Major ID for life sustain.

Guardian (Spear).title: Guardian (Spear)
Guardian (Spear).extract:
Guardian is a level 93 Mythic Spear. It can be found in Loot Chests and dropped by mobs of level 89 to 97.
It is the best +Health weapon in the game, and the third best +Health item in the entire game, only losing to Crusade Sabatons and Statue. It is the best tank weapon for Warrior in the game, and is especially useful when playing in a group (most notably in Raids) due to its Major ID.
Guardian can be Ascended at an Item Upgrader in exchange for various Wards, boosting its combat level to 109, increasing its base damage and Identifications, as well as replacing its Guardian Major ID with an improved version, Heroine's Blessing.

Leo.title: Leo
Leo.extract:
Leo, one of the 12 Zodiac armour pieces, is one of the ideal armour pieces for people with defense or tank builds. Although it has the fourth highest HP boost in the game (only exceeded by Second Wind, Crusade Sabatons and Statue, the latter giving a massive mobility debuff), it's negative water defense makes it not the ideal choice for bosses dealing  Water damage.
Leo provides the fourth highest amount of health in the game with a maximum amount of 6020 HP. The chestplate has no requirements, making it a good HP slap item along with its health regen. Adamantite is used as a substitute to Leo at lower levels.

Olympic.extract:

Discoverer.title: Discoverer
Discoverer.extract:
Discoverer is a level 89 Mythic Chestplate. It can be found in Tier 3 [✫✫✫✫] and Tier 4 [✫✫✫✫] Loot Chests from levels 85 to 93.
It has the best maximum loot bonus stat of any item, beating the runner-up (Jera) by a factor of 4, and beating the next-best chestplate (Diamond Dust) by a factor of 5. As a result, frequent lootrunners value this item immensely. The primary drawback, as referenced in the item lore, is that Discoverer lacks any health stat, making it more difficult to fight mobs or players while wearing one.

Apocalypse.title: Apocalypse
Apocalypse.extract:
Apocalypse is a level 81 Mythic Spear. It can be found in Loot Chests and dropped by mobs of level 77 to 85.
With its negative Health Regen, it slowly drains the wielder's health over time; however, it also yields a huge life steal boost to regain lost health, meaning that mobs must constantly be attacked in order to keep the wielder's health up. Apocalypse also yields large penalties to  Water defense and damage. It can be done to very great extent in Heavy Melee (Stacking as much Main Attack Neutral Damage as possible).
Apocalypse can be Ascended at an Item Upgrader in exchange for various Wards, boosting its combat level to 102, increasing its base damage and Defense requirement, and adding several new Identifications.

The Forgery.title: The Forgery
The Forgery.extract: The Forgery is a dark floating island hovering over the eastern edge of the Light Forest. Due to the sheer altitude of The Forgery, it must be accessed through a teleporter directly below the island. In The Forgery, you can take on Corrupted Dungeons and unlock rewards in the Forgery chest. The main area of The Forgery contains the Forgery chest and a few merchants, including the Key Forge Merchant, who allows players to use Nii Runes, Uth Runes, and Tol Runes to forge Corrupted Dungeon Keys. The area also has Bank access, however it, along with Rymek and Zhight Island, is a bank which does not include an Emerald Merchant. The bank is located outside of the Forgery, and players cannot use it while inside. Players can fast travel to and from all Corrupted Dungeons using teleporters atop The Forgery.

Identifications.title: Identifications
Identifications.extract:
Identifications, or IDs, are bonuses found on a variety of items that can boost or hinder the player in various ways. Identifications can affect damage, defense, mobility, XP gain, and more. Major Identification provide even greater changes to gameplay.
The most common source of identifications is from weapons, armor, and accessories. Armor and accessory identifications are applied as long as they are equipped, while weapon identifications are gained as long as you are holding the weapon. You can also obtain identifications through the effects of potions, tomes, raid buffs, lootrun boons, and crafted consumables from the Alchemism, Cooking, and Scribing professions.
Totals of all currently active identifications can be found by looking at the Character Info menu.

Assassin.title: Assassin
Assassin.extract:
The Assassin is one of the five playable classes in Wynncraft and uses Daggers as its weapon. It has  spells almost exclusive to damage and the unique ability to become invisible in order to escape or attack its enemies easily. The Assassin has a base defense of 100%, which makes it the second most durable class, before the Warrior. The Assassin excels in damage, crowd control, and personal escape, but has a severe lack of range and no health/damage resistance buffs.
For in-depth information on playstyle, tips, and tricks, see the Assassin Guide.

Festival of the Blizzard.title: Festival of the Blizzard
Festival of the Blizzard.extract:
The Festival of the Blizzard is an annual, limited-time seasonal event that coincides with the winter holiday season. It is the third seasonal festival in Wynncraft's cycle of festivals, preceded by the Festivals of the Bonfire and Spirits, and followed by the Festival of the Heroes.
During the event, players are able to obtain exclusive cosmetic items and Pets from Blizzard Crates, similarly to the rewards from regular Loot Crates. Three free Blizzard Crates are available to all players from the start of the event through the Wynncraft Store. Additional crates can be obtained in-game; the first Daily Objective completed each day rewards a Tier I crate, while completing Weekly Objectives, available to players in a level 10+ Guild, rewards a Tier II crate. Up to 30 Blizzard Crates can be obtained for free, while additional crates are available to buy from the Wynncraft Store until the end of the event.
In addition to Blizzard Crates, a winter storm passes over Detlas, redecorating it for the holiday season as Snowy Detlas. The Traveler and Gerald the Yeti are found near the large Craftmas tree in the center of the city, and the Souvenir Sweater Merchant, Rusty Bartender, a Wynnter Owl, a Craftmas Cracker Vendor, and the Confectionery Merchant also set up shop. 
The main activities available during the festival include: inviting other NPCs from around Wynn Province to join in the festivities in Detlas, the Wynnter Fair, which has a variety of minigames and rewards, and the Blizzard Brawl minigame, which is reached by taking the Event Airship Pilot's ship at Detlas Airbase.

Powders.title: Powders
Powders.extract:
Powders are items used to improve armour and weapons. They are based around one of the five Elements in Wynncraft:  Earth,  Thunder,  Water,  Fire, and  Air. There are seven tiers for each of the five types of elemental Powders, with Tier 1 being the weakest and Tier 7 being the strongest.
Powders have a multitude of uses: they can be applied to weapons and armor to give them elemental damage and defense, respectively, and grant powerful powder special effects; they can be upgraded, sold to other players, and transformed into different elements at the Powder Exchange.
For a comprehensive list of all 35 Powders, see here.

Trinkets.title: Trinkets
Trinkets.extract:
Trinkets are items that can be used by any class that provide perks when activated. Trinkets have various ways to obtain them, and are split into two separate categories: Utility Trinkets (with Mobility and Void Trinkets as a subset of these) and Vanity Trinkets. Utility Trinkets provide useful buffs while they are used while Vanity Trinkets provide cosmetic perks without any major utility.
Trinkets can be obtained in various ways, with most being obtainable from Festivals.

Relics.title: Relics
Relics.extract: Relics are special items which can be found in Relic Shrines, places that previously had no use but are nonetheless, points of interest. You can claim various rewards from finding them, like powders, weapons, armour (No accessories yet). They have a cooldown period after finding each one, so it can't be farmed; the above-ground relics, giving some powder or emerald rewards, have a cooldown of four hours, while the hidden relics that give weapons and armour have a cooldown of eight hours.
